stem.text: The temperature T of a metal rod, in degrees Celsius, placed in a chamber held at 55 degrees Celsius moves toward the chamber temperature at a rate proportional to the difference between the chamber temperature and T. At time \( t = 0 \) hours, \( T = 45 \). Using k for the positive constant of proportionality, write a differential equation for T as a function of t and state the initial condition.

worked_solution.text: The dependent variable is T and the independent variable is t in hours, so the rate is \( \frac{dT}{dt} \).

Proportional to the difference means a constant multiple of it. With k positive, \( k(55 - T) \) is positive when T is below 55 and negative when it is above, so T moves up toward 55 from its starting value.
The equation is \( \frac{dT}{dt} = k\left(55 - T\right) \), and the initial condition, stated separately, is \( T(0) = 45 \).

options.label: \( \frac{dT}{dt} = 55 - T \), with \( T(0) = 45 \)
options.derivation: proportional read as equal, so the constant k never appears

options.label: \( \frac{dT}{dt} = k\left(55 - 45\right) \), with \( T(0) = 45 \)
options.derivation: the initial value 45 substituted for T inside the equation, so the rate becomes a constant

options.label: \( \frac{dT}{dt} = k\left(T - 55\right) \), with \( T(0) = 45 \)
options.derivation: the difference written as T minus the level, which with k positive drives T away from 55
